I would not have expected this test to break from this ticket.
You may find this hash-resource logic of interest for example's sake:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/commit/766f392e38e1f1b1a7c4b20026b48e3a682bb8a9

? I think it should be able to handle hash URIs, no?
My mistake, I think your previous statement might be true.
The FedoraLdpIT test was an error on my part. I fixed that. The real problem is in the RDF integration tests.
When I use:
I get a variety of errors because things are not seen as existing.

Failed tests: 
  BibOntologyIT.testExampleRecord:28->AbstractIntegrationRdfIT.createLDPRSAndCheckResponse:63->AbstractIntegrationRdfIT.checkResponse:152 Didn't get a CREATED response! expected:<201> but was:<400>
  GeonameIT.testRoundtripGeonamesRdf:65->AbstractIntegrationRdfIT.createLDPRSAndCheckResponse:63->AbstractIntegrationRdfIT.checkResponse:152 Didn't get a CREATED response! expected:<201> but was:<400>
  ModsRdfIT.testRoundtripModsRDF:165->AbstractIntegrationRdfIT.createLDPRSAndCheckResponse:63->AbstractIntegrationRdfIT.checkResponse:152 Didn't get a CREATED response! expected:<201> but was:<400>
  MusicOntologyIT.testExampleRecord:28->AbstractIntegrationRdfIT.createLDPRSAndCheckResponse:63->AbstractIntegrationRdfIT.checkResponse:152 Didn't get a CREATED response! expected:<201> but was:<400>
  VivoIT.testExampleRecord:28->AbstractIntegrationRdfIT.createLDPRSAndCheckResponse:63->AbstractIntegrationRdfIT.checkResponse:152 Didn't get a CREATED response! expected:<201> but was:<400>
I checked the BibOntologyIT test and this subject
http://localhost:8080/07574fc3-9a8e-4569-9351-5c5536c00fc0#proceedings.pdf
fails the nodeExists test.
The session sees the parent resource
as existing, but not the hash URI.

Hash URIs, like I said, don't exist until they are used, and it's the act of using them that brings them into existence. I'm not sure where that happens, but I think it's somewhere near where you are working now,
I think the check for the "parent" is the right thing to do. The question is just, where to do it. I think it should actually be happening in
HttpResourceConverter
, which would simplify life for clients thereof.
Following on
's work on FCREPO-1411, this now throws the following.

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Date: Thu, 06 Aug 2015 15:53:22 GMT
Link: <http://localhost:8080/static/constraints/IncorrectTripleSubjectException.rdf>; rel="http://www.w3.org/ns/ldp#constrainedBy"
Content-Type: text/plain
Content-Length: 177
Server: Jetty(9.3.1.v20150714)

http://localhost:8080/rest/cdm/ref/collection/chc0015/id/57 is not in the topic of this RDF, which is http://localhost:8080/rest/51/eb/e2/1c/51ebe21c-62aa-452a-8880-cfef670b576f
I just want to confirm that this would not be a correct error to throw for this case?
Actually, the "cuban_postcards.xml" document does indeed suffer from an "incorrect triple subject".
Therefore, maybe this ticket should be closed as resolved by FCREPO-1411.
Thoughts,
Based on the description of the issue in FCREPO-1411, I think this is exactly the same issue and should be considered closed as resolved by it.
Resolved by:
https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-1411
As a follow-on to:
https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-1418

This ticket reveals another example of where a bad RDF document results in a 400 response but is not caught by a "ConstraintExceptionMapper". The following request should result in a <Link; constrainedBy> header that is a URL to a static RDF error description.
curl -i -XPOST -H"Content-Type: application/rdf+xml" --data-binary @cuban_postcards.xml localhost:8080/rest/

comments.body: Andrew Woods can you make a little more precise what is the constraint being violated here?
A. Soroka, I'm thinking that because the subject referenced in the RDF does not exist in the repository. This could be covered by an OutOfDomainSubjectException.

If that's the problem, then I agree with Andrew Woods that this is deserving of a new exception. It's not an OutOfDomainSubjectException because the subject is indeed in-domain, it just doesn't exist. Perhaps something more like NonexistentSubjectException or UncreatedSubjectException.
Sorry, I forgot the IRC conversation the 3 of us had. Looking at my work I was indeed implementing a NoSuchSubjectException.
+1 Jared Whiklo for NoSuchSubjectException.

How do you want to handle Hash URIs? One of the tests now failing with my change is this one in FedoraLdpIT.

I'm assuming we won't test for existence of Hash URIs, but is there a way to test if something is a Hash URI. Other than looking for a hash in it?

I would not have expected this test to break from this ticket.
You may find this hash-resource logic of interest for example's sake:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/commit/766f392e38e1f1b1a7c4b20026b48e3a682bb8a9

Andrew Woods what could be happening here is that a previously-unused hash URI is being used. That's legitimate, but the resource backing that hash URI wouldn't exist yet, so it could appear momentarily as an NoSuchSubjectException kind of thing.

The error stems from trying to use HttpResourceConverter.asString() on a hash URI resource. It returns null.

Not really sure if I can check for existence of a hash URI, but assuming I can would that be the correct way to do it?

So instead I checked for the existence of the "parent" resource.

What I am doing right now in the PersistingRdfConsumer is:

final Resource subject = m.asStatement(t).getSubject();

final int hashIndex = subject.toString().lastIndexOf("#");

final String base_subject = hashIndex > 0 ?
    idTranslator.asString(ResourceFactory.createResource(
    subject.toString().substring(0, hashIndex)))
    : idTranslator.asString(subject);

final boolean in_domain =
   idTranslator.inDomain(subject) || t.getSubject().isBlank();

final boolean subject_exists = (t.getSubject().isBlank() || 
   session.nodeExists(base_subject));
Is this a bug in HttpResourceConverter? I think it should be able to handle hash URIs, no?

My mistake, I think your previous statement might be true. A. Soroka.

The FedoraLdpIT test was an error on my part. I fixed that. The real problem is in the RDF integration tests.

When I use:

final Resource subject = m.asStatement(t).getSubject();

final boolean in_domain =
   idTranslator.inDomain(subject) || t.getSubject().isBlank();

final boolean subject_exists = (t.getSubject().isBlank() || 
   session.nodeExists(subject));

I get a variety of errors because things are not seen as existing.

Failed tests: 
  BibOntologyIT.testExampleRecord:28->AbstractIntegrationRdfIT.createLDPRSAndCheckResponse:63->AbstractIntegrationRdfIT.checkResponse:152 Didn't get a CREATED response! expected:<201> but was:<400>
  GeonameIT.testRoundtripGeonamesRdf:65->AbstractIntegrationRdfIT.createLDPRSAndCheckResponse:63->AbstractIntegrationRdfIT.checkResponse:152 Didn't get a CREATED response! expected:<201> but was:<400>
  ModsRdfIT.testRoundtripModsRDF:165->AbstractIntegrationRdfIT.createLDPRSAndCheckResponse:63->AbstractIntegrationRdfIT.checkResponse:152 Didn't get a CREATED response! expected:<201> but was:<400>
  MusicOntologyIT.testExampleRecord:28->AbstractIntegrationRdfIT.createLDPRSAndCheckResponse:63->AbstractIntegrationRdfIT.checkResponse:152 Didn't get a CREATED response! expected:<201> but was:<400>
  VivoIT.testExampleRecord:28->AbstractIntegrationRdfIT.createLDPRSAndCheckResponse:63->AbstractIntegrationRdfIT.checkResponse:152 Didn't get a CREATED response! expected:<201> but was:<400>

I checked the BibOntologyIT test and this subject
http://localhost:8080/07574fc3-9a8e-4569-9351-5c5536c00fc0#proceedings.pdf
fails the nodeExists test.

The session sees the parent resource
http://localhost:8080/07574fc3-9a8e-4569-9351-5c5536c00fc0
as existing, but not the hash URI.

Hash URIs, like I said, don't exist until they are used, and it's the act of using them that brings them into existence. I'm not sure where that happens, but I think it's somewhere near where you are working now, Jared Whiklo.

I think the check for the "parent" is the right thing to do. The question is just, where to do it. I think it should actually be happening in HttpResourceConverter, which would simplify life for clients thereof.

I just want to confirm that this would not be a correct error to throw for this case?
